discovery: Detection and spectroscopic characterization of exoplanet atmospheres

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: The 2019 Prize recognized the discovery of exoplanets; the nominees turned these points of light into physical worlds whose atmospheres can be measured. Charbonneau observed the first transiting exoplanet and made the first detection of an exoplanet atmosphere (sodium in HD 209458b, 2002). Seager developed the theory of transmission and emission spectra of exoplanet atmospheres that made such measurements possible and interpretable. Snellen pioneered ground-based high-resolution spectroscopy, detecting CO in an exoplanet atmosphere, measuring orbital motion directly and making the first measurement of a planet's rotation. Their methods, combining precise molecular physics with novel observational techniques, now allow routine detection of water, CO, CO2 and other molecules with Hubble, JWST and large ground-based telescopes. This connects the chemistry of planet-forming discs to the composition of mature planets, and so opens a new observational window on planetary origins and habitability.
